card.name: Joining words inside instruction sentences
card.fires_on: Small joining words or commas in the middle of a conditional or cautionary instruction, just before the clause says what to do or what is known. Examples are "until", "as" in "as soon as", "has not", and a comma closing an "if" clause.

modes.label: Until / as soon as
modes.description: A time-linking word that opens a condition on driving, machinery or a missed dose.
modes.example: caution is advised when driving or using machinery<< until>> it is known how the patient reacts to

modes.label: Comma after an if-clause
modes.description: A comma that ends an "if" or "when" clause, just before the action to take.
modes.example: If the level of pain increases after dosage stabilization<<,>> attempt to identify the source of increased pain

modes.label: Has not been investigated
modes.description: The word "not" in a statement that something has not been studied.
modes.example: should not be written on directly since ink migration has<< not>> been investigated.

card.writes: It seems to help the model continue with an impersonal instruction clause and not with a "you" or "we" sentence.
card.plain: It marks the point in a label instruction where the condition is stated and the clause that follows is about to come.
